notes: Extracted from the guide and docs/evidence/transactionstatus.md at e7ed622. The evidence was checked on 0.1.78-c8526ae (25 October); its dbe0e02 section (#394, verified on dbe0e02 and published 28 October) replaces the older sections where they differ, so the older Contract, Web render and Discrepancies lines that say the mark is one “!” in every mode, that Request is the default, that the mark shrinks to 14 px, and that the line runs past a bubble's edge were not used. The guide's Sources were checked on 28 October on the installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). Its TransactionStatus.tsx matches every behaviour the guide states, read from source and its tokens, not run: a tick, a cross or the shared “!” by mode, coloured orange, green, red or grey; an 18 px mark that does not shrink; 4 px, then 12 px text on a 16 px line; one line with a tail ellipsis unless disableTruncation; no press handler. With modes that leave Transaction Status unset, the component sets Expired itself (and TransactionBubble does too), so the generated mode fact's default, Request (the token collection's default), does not apply: the evidence fact on the Transaction Status mode records Expired. With status left out the word comes from the mode's copy token, and Request's is “Expired”, as the evidence says. The guide's “Every Transaction Bubble ends with a Transaction Status” holds for the bubble's default status row only: in the installed TransactionBubble a status slot replaces the line and the chevron; the guide does not say so, so it is not recorded. The guide names no other component to use instead, so the avoidWhen rule (a line that presses, selects or loads) has no useInstead; Biscuit's Storybook page, as the evidence quotes it, also rules out the success screen (StatusHero) and a word-only badge (Badge), and says not to use colour alone; the guide does not say these, so they are not recorded, and accessibility stays empty. Not recorded either: #394's MDX words (Successful, Pending), which the evidence neither marks fixed nor still open now that #394 is closed. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light everywhere), the In context VStack drops the guide's Slot gap M, and the Expired line sets no mode because Expired is the default; the Paid line and the bubbles set the Transaction Status mode because the guide's rule says to set the word and the mode together. The bubbles keep the guide's 231 px width (Figma's bubble width). TransactionBubble has no entry in this pack (rules.md lists it under exports the pack does not cover), but the guide's In context shows the line only inside it, so the thread example keeps it. Dropped: the guide's Request and Declined lines on their own (the thread shows both modes), and the States examples (One line, Wrapped), whose long date “21 October 2026, 4:15 pm” only demonstrates cutting and goes against the content rule to write the date short.

evidenceFacts.name: Transaction Status
evidenceFacts.description: Picks the mark at 18 × 18: Request an orange “!”, Paid a green tick, Declined a red cross, Expired a grey “!”. With no mode the line is the Expired mode: a grey “!” beside “Expired · 20 Mar 2025”.
evidenceFacts.quote: With no mode (or Color Mode Light only) the line is the Expired mode: a grey “!” beside “Expired · 20 Mar 2025” (checked in this run).

gaps.text: Figma's Transaction Status line ends in a chevron; in the package the chevron belongs to TransactionBubble, so a TransactionStatus on its own has none.

from.quote: Figma’s line ends in a chevron; in the package the chevron belongs to Transaction Bubble.

gaps.text: In Figma the mode picks the icon, the colour and the word together; in the package the mode picks the mark, and status and date are free text, so code passes the word.

from.quote: In Figma, Transaction Status is a subcomponent (Coin Subcomponents) with no properties: its mode picks the icon, the colour, and the word together.

gaps.text: The Coin Components Library has no Transaction Status: it is a Coin Subcomponents part that designers meet inside Transaction Bubble.
gaps.quote: There is no Transaction Status in the Coin Components Library: designers meet it inside Transaction Bubble.
